title: CODEX Antibody Staining Protocol for FFPE Tissues
author: Marda Jorgensen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbsdina6

steps.title: Set heating plate to 55 °C
steps.instruction: Turn on the heating plate and set the temperature to 55 °C. Wait until the plate reaches the set temperature.

steps.title: Assemble humidity chamber
steps.instruction: While the wax is melting, construct a humidity chamber from an empty pipette‑tip box with lid: wet a paper towel, place it at the bottom, add enough ddH₂O to cover the towel (≈1–2 cm depth), rinse and dry the tip‑tray, replace it, label positions if using multiple coverslips, and close the lid.

steps.title: Melt wax on coverslips
steps.instruction: Retrieve FFPE samples on poly‑L‑lysine‑treated coverslips from 4 °C storage, place each coverslip tissue‑side up on the hot plate using bent‑tip forceps, and incubate for 20–25 minutes until the paraffin wax is completely melted.

steps.title: Prepare 6‑well reagent plates
steps.instruction: Label 6‑well plates for the number of tissues (e.g., 2 tissues). Add 5.0 ml of the appropriate reagent to each well. For each coverslip allocate: 2 wells of Hydration Buffer (H), 3 wells of Staining Buffer (S), 3 wells of DPBS, and later one well each of PFA and ice‑cold methanol. Allow all reagents to warm to room temperature. Store the empty methanol plate at 4 °C.

steps.title: Cool coverslips in staining rack
steps.instruction: Place the melted‑wax coverslips into a cover‑glass staining rack and let them sit for 5 minutes to cool.

steps.title: Deparaffinize and hydrate tissue
steps.instruction: Perform the following solvent series, immersing the staining rack in each container for 5 minutes. Ensure the coverslips are fully covered, gently move the rack at the start of each step to exchange liquid, and keep the containers closed with lids. Perform in a fume hood.

steps.title: Prepare 1× citrate buffer
steps.instruction: In a 50 ml Pyrex beaker, dilute 100 × citrate buffer (pH 6.0) with ddH₂O to make 40 ml of 1× citrate buffer for each rack of slides.

steps.title: Antigen retrieval in pressure cooker
steps.instruction: Immerse the staining rack in the 1× citrate buffer beaker, wrap the beaker tightly with aluminum foil and seal the rim and spout to prevent water‑vapor entry. Pour 1200 ml DI water into the Instant‑Pot chamber, place the sealed beaker inside, close the lid, set pressure to HIGH, set timer for 20 minutes, turn off the “keep warm” setting, and press PRESSURE COOK to start.

steps.title: Cool and rinse after retrieval
steps.instruction: After the pressure‑cooking cycle ends (≈35–40 min), slowly release the vent, lift the beaker with a hot mitt, and allow the rack to cool on the bench until it is no longer hot. Transfer the rack briefly to a 40 ml beaker of ddH₂O (room temperature) for a few seconds, then move it to a second 40 ml ddH₂O beaker and immerse for 10 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Make CODEX Blocking Buffer
steps.instruction: During the 10‑minute ddH₂O incubation, prepare the CODEX Blocking Buffer by adding Blockers N, G, J, and S to the Staining Buffer in amounts proportional to the number of coverslips being processed.

steps.title: Hydration and staining buffer incubation
steps.instruction: After the 10‑minute ddH₂O step, handle each coverslip with bent‑tip forceps:

substeps.instruction: Place the coverslip in well #1 containing 5 ml Hydration Buffer; incubate 5 seconds.
Transfer to well #2 containing 5 ml Hydration Buffer; incubate 5 seconds.
Transfer to a well containing 5 ml Staining Buffer; incubate 20–30 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare antibody cocktail
steps.instruction: While the coverslips are in the Staining Buffer (STEP 18), add primary barcoded antibodies (1 µl per tissue) to the CODEX Blocking Buffer prepared in STEP 15. Subtract the total antibody volume from the Blocking Buffer volume to keep the final cocktail volume equal to the original Blocking Buffer volume.

steps.title: Add antibody cocktail
steps.instruction: Working one tissue at a time, remove the coverslip from the Staining Buffer, tip to drain, and place it on the humidity chamber. Immediately dispense 190 µl of the antibody cocktail onto a corner of the coverslip (avoid pipetting directly over tissue and avoid bubbles). Cover the humidity chamber lid and incubate at room temperature for 3 hours without disturbance.

steps.title: Add methanol and prepare PFA solution
steps.instruction: At 2.5 hours into the antibody incubation:

substeps.instruction: Add 5.0 ml ice‑cold methanol to a pre‑labeled 6‑well plate (one well per coverslip) and keep the plate on ice.
Prepare PFA solution on ice: mix 1.0 ml of 16 % PFA with 9.0 ml of storage buffer, then aliquot 5.0 ml into a well of a labeled 6‑well plate for each coverslip.
Lift each coverslip from the humidity chamber, tip to drain, and place in Staining Buffer well #1 of a second cluster dish; incubate 2 minutes.
Transfer to Staining Buffer well #2 of the same dish; incubate 2 minutes.
Transfer to the PFA well; incubate 10 minutes.
Transfer sequentially to PBS well #1, #2, and #3, immersing the coverslip 2–3 times in each.
Transfer to the ice‑cold methanol well; incubate 5 minutes on ice.

steps.title: Prepare final fix solution
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw CODEX Final Fix Reagent, spin briefly, then add 20 µl of Final Fix to 1.0 ml of PBS and mix thoroughly (room temperature).

steps.title: Apply final fix to coverslips
steps.instruction: Quickly transfer each coverslip to a clean humidity chamber, add 190 µl of the final‑fix solution to a corner of the coverslip, and incubate at room temperature for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Store stained coverslips
steps.instruction: Place each coverslip tissue‑side up in a labeled well containing 5.0 ml Storage Buffer, wrap the edges of the 6‑well plate with parafilm, and store at 4 °C. Record the date; stained tissue is stable for up to 2 weeks.
